title: Logic Drummer Tricks
intro: Drummer is not a loop library. It plays a performance you can steer, and its kick and snare can follow the rhythm of another track in your project — a different one for each region if you like.

tips.t: Use Complexity and Intensity, then the kit-piece sliders
tips.d: In the Session Player Editor, drag the Complexity slider up for a busier part and the Intensity slider up for a louder one. Apple lists both as settings common to all Session Players, Drummer included. Then click Details and drag the kit piece sliders to set the complexity range of individual kit pieces.

tips.t: Change the drummer, not just the preset
tips.d: If a preset is close but the feel is wrong, try other presets or drummers. Lock the fills first if you like them: Apple says the lock stops 'any changes to the fills setting when switching presets or drummers.'

tips.t: Turn individual kit pieces on and off per region
tips.d: Click a kit piece in the editor to enable or disable it for that region only. Drop the crash out of the verse and back in for the chorus.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Drummer performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Convert a Drummer region to MIDI and edit it by hand
tips.d: Right‑click the region and choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. You get the full performance in the Piano Roll to nudge, delete and re‑velocity as you like.

src.label: Apple — Convert Session Player regions into MIDI or pattern regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use the Details panel for feel, ghost notes and hi‑hat
tips.d: Click the Details button in the Drummer Editor to reveal Feel (drag right to play ahead of the beat, left to play behind it), Ghost Notes (syncopated snare and kick hits), Hi-Hat openness and Humanize. This is where a stiff pattern becomes a groove.

src.label: Apple — Edit a Drummer performance in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Swap and tune kit pieces in Drum Kit Designer
tips.d: In Drum Kit Designer, click a kit piece to open its Edit and Exchange panes. Swap the kick or snare (toms, cymbals and hi-hat too on multi-channel kits) and set Tune, Dampen (sustain) and Gain per piece. Multi-channel kits add Overheads and Room (A, B or off) switches.
